start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:name-the-recording-behind-transcript-lines with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and ranges [\"12-40\", \"90-95\"]." It tells you which recording lines 12 to 40 and 90 to 95 come from, and where in it.
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: the archive windows are the person's own rows in their own store, in whatever form that store keeps them, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the archive windows are kept and how the store is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:name-the-recording-behind-transcript-lines" with store and the line ranges, each first-last.
3. The first run makes the window rows once and proves the lookup on the example windows: every expected answer must match, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run names the recording and first words of each window that overlaps each range you give, and says which ranges overlap none.

worked_examples.title: Which recording lines 12 to 40 come from
worked_examples.ask: Lines 12 to 40 of my transcript archive: which recording is that?

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the archive windows kept in the person's database; the prove step matched every expected answer.
worked_examples.hands_back: Three windows: h1 of Harbour talk lines 1 to 50, m1 of Market walk lines 1 to 30, and m2 of Market walk lines 31 to 60, each with its first words.

worked_examples.title: A range that starts after it ends is refused

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The range ends before it starts.
worked_examples.hands_back: Refused: the range 9-3 ends before it starts, so write the smaller line number first, for example 3-9.
